metadata.case_name: RUKHSAR BEGUM v. NATIVE ENGLISH CENTER LTD T/A THE GREEN LOUNGE

plaintiff.expected_occupation_after: office clerk, a cashier or a receptionist
plaintiff.education_level: educated in Hong Kong up to Form 5

injuries.description: fracture of the base of the distal phalanx of the right ring finger (healed with mild mal-union)
source: there was in fact a fracture of the base of the distal phalanx of the finger even though the fracture had already healed quite well with mild mal-union at the time of his review of the films. The mal-union, in Dr Li’s opinion, may potentially cause residual symptoms.

injuries.description: meniscal tear of the right knee (classified as "grade 2"; MRI reported "possible tear of posterior horn of medical meniscus")
source: It was stated in the MRI report that the knee had a “possible tear of posterior horn of medical meniscus”.
Dr Li classified the meniscal tear of the right knee as “grade 2”.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injuries to the knee or lower leg

source: She was found by the physiotherapist to have suffered from “right traumatic patellar tendinitis”.
injuries.icd_description: Injury of other specified muscle, fascia, tendon or bursa at lower leg level

manifestations.description: tender and swollen right ring finger with reduced range of movement
tender and swollen right knee with reduced range of movement
right knee pain (complained for first 2 months after the accident; ongoing mild discomfort)
limping gait and could walk unaided for about 15 minutes (by December 2013)
discomfort from continuous bending or standing for 4 hours or more
mild stiffness of right ring finger

treatments_received.treatment: treated and discharged with a knee brace and walking stick on the same day
source: She was treated and discharged with a knee brace and walking stick on the same day.

treatments_received.treatment: follow-up sessions with the Orthopaedics & Traumatology Department (Queen Mary Hospital) on 2 December 2013, 24 February 2014, 3 March 2014 and 23 June 2014
source: Upon referral, Ms Begum attended four follow-up sessions with the Orthopaedics & Traumatology Department (“O & T”) of Queen Mary Hospital on 2 December 2013, 24 February, 3 March and 23 June 2014.

treatments_received.treatment: physiotherapy (two sessions) on 16 December 2013 and 23 December 2013
source: and two physiotherapy treatments for her knee injury on 16 and 23 December 2013.

treatments_received.treatment: MRI scan of the right knee (private) on 15 January 2014
source: On 15 January 2014, Ms Begum had an MRI scan of the right knee done privately. It was stated in the MRI report that the knee had a “possible tear of posterior horn of medical meniscus”.

treatments_future.treatment: exercises at home with the use of a gadget called "Power Putty"
source: Dr Li recommended Ms Begum to undergo conservative treatment to strengthen the finger function by doing exercises at home with the use of a gadget called “Power Putty” (at the total cost of $450 for the entire set).
In Li’s 1st, 12 sessions are being recommended.

treatments_future.treatment: non-surgical conservative treatment for the right knee (as opined by Dr Li)
source: Dr Li opined in Li’s 2nd that Ms Begum should recover the normal strength and endurance of the knee by non-surgical conservative treatment.

losses.description: Unable to resume her pre-accident waitressing job due to residual pain; Dr Li opined the meniscal tear will make it difficult for her to return to her pre-accident job as a waitress.
Discomfort from continuous bending or standing for 4 hours or more, limiting ability to stand for prolonged periods.

comparable_cases.injury_description: fracture of a tibial plateau and a lateral meniscal tear; had an operation
